articles.title: Updated 2026 MLB Playoffs Bracket Picture and Standings After Brewers Clinch NL Central
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers already punched their ticket to the MLB playoffs for the eighth time in nine years, and on Tuesday they won the National League Central with a 5-1 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers already punched their ticket to the MLB playoffs for the eighth time in nine years, and on Tuesday they won the National League Central with a 5-1 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates.

The NL Central champions own the league's best record (94-57) and own a 10-game lead on the second-place Chicago Cubs within the division.

MLB playoff picture after two more teams clinch

The Brewers have clearly found a formula for success in the regular season. Their current run has outlasted a managerial change, the departure of lead executive David Stearns and the exits of key players.

Every year, Milwaukee promotes more homegrown talent to the majors and fills out the roster around the margins.

The overall concern this season is the same as it has been in the past. Put the Brewers up against a franchise with more stars or a far bigger payroll and they could hit their ceiling.

Milwaukee finished four games better than the Los Angeles Dodgers in the 2025 regular season, but the NLCS came down to the fact the Dodgers had better top-end talent. Shohei Ohtani, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow combined to allow two earned runs, and Ohtani had four RBI in the series. L.A. swept the NL's No. 1 seed aside.

Jacob Misiorowski had a solid postseason debut, going 2-1 with a 1.50 ERA and 16 strikeouts in 12 innings, and he has only improved on the mound in 2026. The right-hander is likely headed toward a Cy Young Award.

There isn't another dominant bona fide ace in the rotation, though, and midseason acquisition Dustin May has regressed badly after his trade from the St. Louis Cardinals.

It's a similar story with the offense. Collectively, the Brewers have one of the best lineups in baseball. But the likes of Brice Turang, Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers and William Contreras are all very good without fully cracking into the elite tier as hitters.

Maybe this is when the stars align for the Brewers, and they've long shed the label of underdogs. They have the second-best World Series odds (+600) at FanDuel Sportsbook .

Should the team miss out on a National League pennant once again, the front office may have to give serious thought to getting aggressive and pushing in some chips to get over the hump.

articles.title: MLB power rankings: Brewers, Rays, Dodgers take the top 3 spots as the playoffs approach
articles.summary: Our final rankings of the regular season highlight each team's MVP, from Jacob Misiorowski to Hunter Goodman.
articles.body:
The regular season is winding down, with the teams at the top of the standings starting to clinch their spots in the postseason and those at the bottom being mathematically eliminated .

Our latest power rankings — the final edition of this regular season, as our next rankings will include only the 12 teams that qualify for October — take one final look back and determine each team's regular-season MVP.

Jump to a team by clicking on the links below:

AL Central: White Sox | Guardians | Tigers | Twins | Royals

NL Central: Brewers | Cubs | Pirates | Cardinals | Reds

There's no shortage of statistics highlighting Jacob Misiorowski 's glow-up from dynamic rookie with sky-high potential to maybe (probably?) The Best Pitcher On The Planet. But here's a simple one exemplifying how unhittable The Miz has been: Batters are hitting .156 against Misiorowski this season, which would be the lowest mark for a qualified starting pitcher in a full season in MLB history, besting the record held by 2000 Pedro Martinez at .167. Martinez finished fifth in AL MVP voting that season; it'll be interesting to see where Misiorowski ends up on NL MVP ballots come season's end.

Can Junior Caminero make a late charge past Yordan Alvarez for AL MVP? He's got a classic case as the best player on the best team, and he delivered his signature moment on Friday , when his walk-off homer (against Alvarez's Astros , no less) clinched a playoff berth for Tampa Bay and his second consecutive 40-homer season. And while Caminero's defense at the hot corner doesn't grade out well, his durability and availability have been admirable: He has started every single game at third for the Rays . Only Matt Olson has played more defensive innings this season. Whether he catches Alvarez or not, there's no disputing that Caminero is the heart and soul of the American League's runaway No. 1 seed, and he'll have the opportunity to elevate his profile even further in October.

Don't let his first trip to the injured list as a Dodger overshadow what Shohei Ohtani was able to accomplish before he went down. While the sequencing and drawn-out nature of his injury saga raised some big questions for the Dodgers and Ohtani with October approaching, he still provided an immense amount of value before his pitching was paused and his offensive performance tailed off, including a .902 OPS with 30 homers at the plate and a 1.79 ERA across 85 ⅔ innings pitched. He might not win MVP for the first time in four years, but there's a great chance that Ohtani still finishes second, and it's hard to argue against that runner-up placement based on how spectacular he was in the first half of the season.

After all he accomplished in Chicago and Boston , Chris Sale has somehow leveled up again since joining the Braves, even as he enters his late-30s. Most remarkable has been Sale's rediscovery of the high-end velocity that he hadn't showcased in nearly a decade, pushing his fastball up to triple-digits in Atlanta's marquee matchup with the Dodgers last month. Back spasms prevented Sale from pitching for the Braves in the playoffs two years ago, and the team missed October last year. So whether it be in the wild-card round or the division series, Sale's upcoming postseason debut for Atlanta will be one of the most highly anticipated outings of October.

With three-time MVP Aaron Judge sidelined for multiple months, it's the pitching that has carried the Yankees into a comfortable position in the standings, and sophomore right-hander Cam Schlittler has been at the forefront of those efforts. Schlittler's electric postseason debut last October sparked sizable hype entering his first full season in the Yankees' rotation, and he has more than delivered on those lofty expectations. Schlittler leans heavily on three hellacious, high-90s fastball variants (44% four-seam, 25% cutter, 20% sinker) to utterly overwhelm opposing batters, and his brilliance has started to build some MVP buzz .

It has been a strange season for Cristopher Sánchez . The bad: He has allowed 10-plus hits on five occasions; no other pitcher in MLB has more than three such outings. The good: Sánchez has gone at least six innings with zero earned runs allowed 11 times this year; that's three more than any other pitcher. On the whole, it has been another ace-like campaign, and Sánchez ranks third in fWAR among starting pitchers , behind only Cy Young frontrunners Misiorowski and Schlittler. Even in a rotation with several other frontline arms, Sánchez stands out.

Alex Bregman has been one of the most valuable players in baseball for the past three months , which would earn him the nod here on most other rosters. But Bregman's teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong has spent that same span of time absolutely lapping the field in WAR and most offensive categories amid one of the best seasons in Cubs franchise history — and the Cubs have been around for a while! Crow-Armstrong's astonishing ascension from young superstar to full-blown main character of the major leagues cannot be overstated. This has been the regular season of PCA; will his storybook season continue in October?

On the morning of May 30, Fernando Tatis Jr. woke up with a .652 OPS and zero home runs through 236 plate appearances across 55 games. Since then, he has hit .300/.364/.546 with 22 homers and 21 stolen bases in 93 games, accruing 4.3 fWAR along the way, the second-highest mark in MLB over that span behind only PCA. Need I say more?

Willson Contreras has far surpassed even the most optimistic expectations for his first year in Boston, posting a career-best 151 wRC+ that ranks third among qualified hitters, behind only Crow-Armstrong and Yordan Alvarez. As hoped, his offensive profile has fit perfectly at Fenway Park, where he has hit .323/.429/.581 compared to .232/.345/.455 away from Boston. And beyond the batting, Contreras' unwavering intensity and competitiveness set the tone for the Red Sox on and off the field as they rallied back up the standings after a poor start to the season.

He doesn't have the gaudy power numbers of some of the other top backstops in baseball, but there's a case to be made that Gabriel Moreno has been the best all-around catcher in the majors this season. Among the 26 primary catchers with at least 300 plate appearances, Moreno's 13 homers are tied for 15th, but he's first in batting average (.301), first in on-base percentage (.379), second in wRC+ (133) and ninth among qualified catchers in Statcast's Fielding Run Value. He's often overshadowed by some of the bigger names in the Snakes' lineup, but if Arizona manages to eke out a wild-card spot, Moreno will be a massive reason for it.

After arriving via trade two years ago, when the White Sox had one of the worst offenses in modern baseball history — which he contributed to with a .387 OPS over 42 games down the stretch — Miguel Vargas has blossomed into a legitimate offensive force as the centerpiece of the upstart White Sox lineup. He swatted his 31st homer of the season on Monday in Chicago's crucial victory over Cleveland to claim the tiebreaker in the AL Central race. Most impressive is that Vargas' sterling underlying batted-ball data fully supports his breakout: While his .361 wOBA ranks 29th among qualified batters, his .381 xwOBA ranks eighth .

As with Aaron Judge and the Yankees lineup, José Ramírez — the perennial leading candidate for Guardians' MVP — going down in June due to a hamate injury (and struggling to produce after returning) opened the door for others on Cleveland 's roster to emerge as headlining contributors. Seizing that opportunity have been a trio of standout rookies in Parker Messick , Chase DeLauter and Travis Bazzana. All three have enjoyed stretches of excellence buoying Cleveland's push for a postseason spot, but Messick's steadiness atop the rotation has been especially impressive. Not only is he making a run for AL Rookie of the Year, but also the 25-year-old southpaw has a real chance of finishing as the third AL Cy Young finalist behind leading contenders Schlittler and Dylan Cease .

His chances at claiming the Triple Crown have dwindled as he has cooled off a bit in September, and he might be managing an ankle injury with October approaching, but Yordan Alvarez has been head-and-shoulders above every other hitter in the league from a pure offensive standpoint this season, at a whopping 175 wRC+ (.310/.427/.589), and he might earn his first AL MVP Award as a result. If anything, his dominance has been a reminder of what Houston was missing last season, when he played only 48 games and the Astros missed the postseason for the first time since 2016.

Ezequiel Durán has quietly delivered one of the great superutility seasons in recent history, appearing in at least 10 games at every position besides first base, catcher and pitcher. Incredibly, his glovework has graded out as average or better at every spot, including a remarkable +12 Outs Above Average across 385 innings at shortstop while Corey Seager was sidelined. All the while, Duran has enjoyed a career season at the plate, setting personal bests in doubles (26), homers (17), RBI (80) and wRC+ (117).

Where would the Blue Jays be had they not shelled out a hefty chunk of change last offseason to sign Dylan Cease ? The rest of their rotation has been ravaged by injuries, and those woes combined with the disappointing offense led Toronto to trade away its only other reliable rotation arm, Kevin Gausman , with an eye toward the future. But as the Blue Jays have continued to hang around the wild-card race, Cease has stayed steady as the one of premier right-handers in the league, racking up a career-high 236 strikeouts and yielding more weak contact than ever when he's not coaxing whiffs.

Bryan Reynolds has been the steadiest Bucco bat, having appeared in every game for Pittsburgh this year, but Brandon Lowe has felt like this club's biggest difference-maker on the whole, ahead of even the rotation filled with talented arms. Lowe has supplied pop as planned — his 29 homers are the most by a Pirate since Josh Bell in 2019 (37) — but his shockingly good (and much improved) defense at the keystone (+14 Outs Above Average) has made his addition all the more impactful. He's an intriguing free agent to monitor this winter .

WAR metrics that favor defensive contributions will tell you that rookie JJ Wetherholt and his sparkling glovework at second base have been the best all-around player for St. Louis this year, but the most important development for the Cardinals in 2026 has been the offensive breakout of 24-year-old Jordan Walker . Walker now looks like the kind of slugger you can build a lineup around, a foundational piece who can anchor the offense as St. Louis tries to restore its status as a contender. Plus, Walker's Home Run Derby performance in Philadelphia was arguably the highlight of this entire Cardinals season, alongside Joshua Baez's historic debut .

DFA'd by the Giants at the start of the 2024 season after debuting briefly with Toronto, Otto Lopez has developed into an all-around menace with the Fish, making his first All-Star Game this summer and leading the majors in hits with less than two weeks to go. And if the bat-to-ball skills weren't enough, Lopez is also a stellar defender at shortstop and one of the most impactful baserunners in the league. What a fun and valuable player he has become.

Pete Alonso 's emotional homecoming in Queens this week was an emphatic reminder of how much he and his rock-solid production have been missed in the Mets ' lineup. He has continued to be a dependable force atop the batting order for his new ballclub, roughly replicating his terrific output from his final season as a Met while starting every game for the Orioles, with his durability remaining a hallmark of his profile. It might not be enough to fuel a return to October, but Alonso has done his part and then some in his first year in Birdland.

This is a toss-up between Dillon Dingler and Kevin McGonigle , as Dingler was unbelievable on both sides of the ball until a shockingly ice-cold stretch in August did some serious damage to his overall statline. McGonigle has been awfully consistent all season, which is no small feat as a 21-year-old rookie. His special hit tool has largely lived up to the significant preseason hype while he has spent the bulk of his defensive reps at shortstop. McGonigle has thus far been everything Detroit could've hoped for and an ideal piece to build around in the post-Tarik Skubal Era.

A hamate injury cost Ryan Jeffers a couple of months in the middle of the season, but what the 29-year-old catcher has shown when available (137 wRC+) should make him one of the more attractive position players available in free agency this offseason . And with the Twins having just drafted their next potential franchise catcher in Vahn Lackey, it's likely that Jeffers will begin a new chapter elsewhere after a stellar tenure in Minnesota since he was selected in the second round back in 2018.

Like Cleveland, the good parts of the Mets' season have largely been defined by rookies , in their case an ace in Nolan McLean and a pair of dynamic outfielders in Carson Benge and AJ Ewing. But on a pitching staff where so much else went wrong, McLean establishing himself as a frontline arm (or close to it) has been especially encouraging, and he just might pitch himself to NL Rookie of the Year honors with a few strong outings to close out the season.

Randy Arozarena has been the only consistent bright spot in an otherwise disastrous season for Seattle, an on-base machine full of clutch moments that have far too often been undone by shortcomings elsewhere on the roster. Arozarena has timed his fantastic campaign well, as he has played himself onto the short list of best position players available in a relatively weak free-agent class this winter. He should cash in accordingly.

Last year, Elly De La Cruz played all 162 games but was reportedly battling a left quad injury for most of the season, which hampered his performance. This season, De La Cruz made his first trip to the injured list as a big leaguer due to a hamstring strain in June but has otherwise delivered exactly the kind of step forward many were hoping for last year. This more healthy version of De La Cruz has been an all-around dynamo on both sides of the ball, and his gigantic improvement batting from the right side as a switch-hitter could be what unlocks his true MVP potential moving forward, even beyond his annual crown as Cincinnati's best player.

The surface-level stats — 30 homers and an NL-leading .395 on-base percentage — are plenty impressive on their own, but it's the underlying batted-ball data that solidifies James Wood as one of the most dangerous sluggers in the league. Wood stands alone atop the leaderboards for average exit velocity (95.1 mph), hard-hit rate (58.1%) and barrel rate (20.1%), process-oriented metrics that support the eye test suggesting he'll be terrorizing opposing pitchers for the foreseeable future. What a hitter.

Rafael Devers ' season is suddenly over after the Giants placed him on the 60-day injured list Sunday due to a core muscle injury that might require surgery, but it was hard to tell he was battling through anything based on his recent production. Devers hit .377/.476/.928 (1.403 OPS) with 11 HR over his final 18 games before being sidelined. His final tally of 37 homers is the most by a Giant in the post-Barry Bonds era, far exceeding Willy Adames ' 30 from a year ago. A lot went wrong in San Francisco this year , but Devers' first full season as a Giant was a smashing success.

You'd be forgiven for thinking Bobby Witt Jr. was having a down season because of how far off the radar the Royals have been, but his sensational defense at shortstop (22 Outs Above Average) and overall offensive production (121 wRC+, 40 stolen bases) have combined for 6.5 fWAR, the top mark in the AL. Witt winning the AL MVP Award this year for the first time would be something of a surprise considering his modest slugging output (18 HR) and lack of national relevance on a last-place team, but another finish on or near the proverbial podium is in play and would be deserved.

A poor pitching staff and an avalanche of injuries in the lineup sunk this A's season by midsummer. But Henry Bolte has been a rare bright spot and a late-rising candidate for team MVP. For the purposes of this exercise, I'll give the rookie outfielder the nod, and not only to celebrate the nominative determinism of the guy named Bolte (pronounced bol-TAY, to be fair) being atop this season's sprint speed leaderboard . Since Aug. 1, Bolte is hitting .312/.397/.497 and leading American League position players in fWAR . That's ridiculous!

Reid Detmers is the objectively correct pick here — he should fetch a ton in a trade if the Angels finally choose to deal him this winter — but allow me to salute Mike Trout for playing 130-plus games in consecutive seasons for the first time since 2018-19 and continuing to produce at a well above-average clip while regularly manning center field at age 34 and now 35. Even with his best days so clearly behind him, Trout ranks third in OBP among qualified AL hitters, behind only Alvarez and Contreras.

Catcher Hunter Goodman has demonstrated that his 2025 breakout was no fluke, repeating as the Rockies' lone All-Star representative and upping his home run total from 31 to 38 (with two weeks to go). And before you cry "Coors!" regarding his gaudy dinger count, consider this: 23 of Goodman's long balls have come away from Colorado. That's the second-most road homers in a single season by a Rockie behind only 1997 Larry Walker, with 29!

images.caption: Jacob Misiorowski is Milwaukee's MVP and the likely NL Cy Young winner. Will he also receive NL MVP votes? (Bruno Rouby/Yahoo Sports)

articles.title: SeaWolves ready to begin their fifth straight post season
articles.summary: Crowds filled the stands at UPMC Park as the Erie SeaWolves began another postseason. The Minor League Baseball team has reached a milestone, making the play...
articles.body:
Crowds filled the stands at UPMC Park as the Erie SeaWolves began another postseason.

The Minor League Baseball team has reached a milestone, making the playoffs for five straight years. It was a special night at UPMC Park, game one of the playoffs.

The SeaWolves are no stranger to their first-round opponents, the Richmond Flying Squirrels, but fans Tuesday night were hoping for a win for our home team.

"We had people here at nine am working hard and getting everything ready, from hospitality areas to on the field and the grounds crew working, so we're all getting our hours in and making sure UPMC Park is ready for this game one of the Southwest Division Series," said Laina Banic, the marketing director for the Erie SeaWolves.

The very last possible home game of the season is potentially Sunday if they win the Southwest Division. Then they would move on to play the Northeast winner.

articles.title: Kyle Schwarber, Colson Montgomery Have Chance To Break Not So Great MLB Record
articles.summary: Not all Major League Baseball Records are great to own
articles.body:
Colson Montgomery of the Chicago White Sox and Kyle Schwarber both have a chance to break the single-season strikeout record this year.

The record for strikeouts in a season by a batter is 223 strikeouts, set by Mark Reynolds in 2009. It's not a glamorous record to own, but it does not always mean a player had a terrible season. Over the years, many players have come close to beating Reynolds' record. Most recently, James Wood struck out 221 times last year, but had an .825 OPS and 31 home runs.

This year, Schwarber is at 210 strikeouts, and Montgomery is at 209. Montgomery struck out a bunch last year as well, but had a .840 OPS in 71 games. This year, his OPS is .712. However, he has been an important player for the Chicago White Sox, blasting 31 home runs in their unexpected season.

Schwarber has had the kind of season that makes teams completely forget about the strikeouts. He has a league-leading 44 home runs and an .869 OPS. Reynolds hit 44 home runs during his 2009 season.

Montgomery and the White Sox and Schwarber and the Phillies each have 12 games left this season. Both have a real chance to break Reynolds' record, but they have already put together great seasons. Their success, despite the strikeouts, is a glimpse into the modern offensive philosophy. Every team is chasing the long ball and is more willing to look past strikeouts.

articles.title: Carlos Correa Injury Update Reveals Astros Star's Status for Rest of MLB Season Amid Ankle Issue
articles.summary: The Houston Astros will be without their star shortstop for the remainder of the year.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros will be without their star shortstop for the remainder of the year.

Astros manager Joe Espada told reporters Tuesday that Carlos Correa will be out for the rest of the season amid an ankle issue that has sidelined him for most of the year.

Correa underwent surgery on his left ankle in May and faced a return timeline of six to eight months. He was initially set to miss the remainder of the season , but there was optimism as of late that he could make a return before the postseason.

The Athletic's Chandler Rome reported Tuesday that Correa planned to return to the team's spring training facility in Florida this week to meet with doctors and potentially receive clearance for a rehab assignment with Triple-A Sugar Land.

Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic noted last week that if Correa was able to return, the team was considering putting him at second base. He has only ever played at third base and shortstop in his career.

But the Astros' hopes of getting the three-time All-Star back on the field have seemingly now been squashed, and they'll have to continue their playoff push without him.

"The most important thing for him now is to focus on next season," Espada told reporters .

Espada said Correa did not suffer a setback in his recovery, but the rehab took a toll on his leg and ankle and created soreness.

In 32 games before his injury, Correa had hit three home runs and 16 RBI while slashing .279/.369/.418.

The Astros are currently sitting atop the AL West at 75-75, but they are just one game ahead of the second-place Texas Rangers. Houston will take on the Kansas City Royals starting Tuesday after being swept by the Tampa Bay Rays over the weekend.

articles.title: Astros manager Joe Espada confirms SS Carlos Correa will not return from ankle injury this season
articles.summary: Correa had been sidelined since May 4 due to a torn tendon in his ankle.
articles.body:
Houston Astros manager Joe Espada confirmed to reporters Tuesday that shortstop Carlos Correa will not return this season. Correa has been sidelined since the beginning of May due to an ankle injury. When the injury occurred, it was expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season.

In early August, however, Espada said Correa had been cleared to resume swinging a bat. The shortstop was expected to go out on a rehab assignment in the near future, with a chance to return before the postseason.

Espada said Tuesday that Correa has not suffered a setback or another injury that is preventing him from returning this year. Instead, the manager said the "daily workload" and the "recovery" became too much for the veteran shortstop.

Correa had been cleared for swinging and had begun taking ground balls at second base. Houston was trying to find a way to get him back into the lineup alongside Jeremy Peña at shortstop and Isaac Paredes at third, Correa's typical positions.

Correa initially tore a tendon in his ankle in a freak batting practice accident. Before the injury, he played in 32 games for Houston. The shortstop was slashing .279/.369/.418 with three home runs and 16 RBI.

The 31-year-old veteran is playing on a six-year, $200 million deal that he originally signed with the Minnesota Twins . Minnesota traded him back to Houston ahead of the 2025 trade deadline. The Astros have two more years of Correa on their books, and Houston has four club options between 2029 and 2032.

Correa has a history of ankle injuries. He had two free-agent megadeals with the San Francisco Giants and the New York Mets fall through due to concerns about his ankle's health. Those were about his right ankle, though; this torn tendon is in the shortstop's left ankle.

As of Tuesday, Houston has a 75-75 record and a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Correa will now turn his attention to getting fully healthy for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Rare Mickey Mantle Photo from 1951 Sells for $3M, More Than Doubles Record
articles.summary: A rare photo of New York Yankees legend Mickey Mantle sold for a historic price on Tuesday.
articles.body:
A rare photo of New York Yankees legend Mickey Mantle sold for a historic price on Tuesday.

Per The Athletic's Larry Holder , a photo of the Hall of Famer from 1951 sold for a record-breaking price of $3 million in a private sale brokered by Hunt Auctions.

The unsigned photo of Mantle was used for his iconic 1952 Topps baseball card and is PSA Type I authenticated. The sale shattered the record for an autographed sports photo, which was previously held by a Shoeless Joe Jackson signed image sold by Christie's and Hunt Auctions in 2021 for $1.47 million.

Holder noted that a PSA Type I photo is "a first generation photograph, developed from the original negative, during the period (within approximately two years of when the picture was taken)."

Hunt Auctions said that the photo sold of Mantle was initially used by the International News Service in a local news release and was not used for national distribution.

"The demand for high-end original Type I photographs from new collectors and investors coming into the space is at an all-time high," said PSA photo authenticator Henry Yee, per Holder. "The supply however for this material is extremely scarce. When an item of this caliber is offered for sale, often it is sold privately and does not even make it to public auction — such as in this case."

Mantle was a 20-time All-Star and three-time MVP who won seven World Series with the New York Yankees during his 18-year career. He retired in 1968 and died in 1995.

articles.title: MLB World Series favorite faces serious trouble as the regular season enters its final few weeks of the year
articles.summary: Dodgers’ three-peat hopes threatened by Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Andy Pages injuries as Edwin Diaz struggles entering 2026 season’s final stretch.
articles.body: Somehow, there are just two weeks remaining in the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season. Once again, this baseball season has shown how and why trying to predict it remains one of the most futile endeavors in sports. And that lack of predictability is even more apparent as several postseason races look set to come down to the last few games of the season. The American League playoff race has several spots up for grabs, with teams hoping to avoid the wrong kind of history: becoming the first sub-.500 team to reach the postseason in a full season. While the Chicago White Sox have led the American League Central for most of the season, the Cleveland Guardians are just 1.5 games back with two games remaining in their series on Tuesday and Wednesday. WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW In the AL West, the Houston Astros are clinging to a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers at 75-75, though the teams don't play each other the rest of the year. Then there's the wild card race. The Guardians currently sit in the third wild card position at 76-75, but the Toronto Blue Jays, left for dead months ago, have clawed their way back into it, just one game back. If the Rangers can’t catch the Astros, they’re still just 1.5 games back of the third wild-card spot. Even the 73-78 Baltimore Orioles are only three games behind Cleveland. Somehow. So there are two teams competing for the AL Central, two teams competing for the AL West and four competing for the final wild card spot behind the Yankees and Red Sox. Those division races will also determine which team gets a first-round bye and who's forced into a best-of-three wild card series. Cleveland, Chicago, Houston and Texas are all within just a few games of each other, meaning that the second and third seed might not be determined until the final weekend. Hilariously, there are just five teams with a positive run differential in the AL, and one of them, the Tigers, is 71-79 and effectively eliminated. On the NL side, there are just two teams fighting for the final wild card spot, the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Diego Padres. While the Padres have become baseball's hottest team, Arizona's still just 2.5 games behind. More importantly, those two teams play each other in the final series with the season tiebreaker up for grabs, meaning that the race may not be clinched until literally the last day of the year. Last game, two division rivals potentially playing for a postseason berth at Petco Park. A dream scenario for the league. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Speaking of the west, while the Dodgers have clinched a postseason berth, they're still battling with the Braves to clinch the second seed behind the runaway Milwaukee Brewers. And that bye might be even more important than it normally is, because the Dodgers are in trouble. Serious trouble. While they've accumulated a tremendous amount of talent between their player development, fortuitous trades and their obviously large financial advantages, much of it is far from full strength heading into October. And it might cost them a chance at a three-peat. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Shohei Ohtani is on the injured list for the first time as a Dodger, after dealing with knee and arm injuries for most of the season. Not only will he not be available to pitch in the playoffs, he won't be eligible to return until the final weekend of the season. Freddie Freeman has been battling right knee soreness severe enough to keep him out of the lineup several times over the past week. Andy Pages, who's been one of the Dodgers most valuable players this season, fractured his hand on a hit by pitch several weeks ago and, while he's started taking swings, has no set return date before the postseason. Then there's Edwin Díaz. Díaz, who signed for $69 million in the offseason, went from a 1.63 ERA in 2025 to 11.85 in 2026. He went down for several months with an arm injury himself, only to return and look... worse. One of the most expensive relief pitchers in baseball has seven saves and four blown saves, allowing a remarkable 37 baserunners and 18 runs in 13.2 innings. He's back on the injured list, and just gave up five runs in a rehab appearance in the minor leagues. Edgardo Henriquez, who's helped fill in for Díaz at the back end of the bullpen, has been outstanding over the last month. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Except he's now hurt too, going on the injured list with back issues that will keep him out for the remainder of the regular season. Roki Sasaki too, had gone on the IL and was expected back this past weekend, only for manager Dave Roberts to say Tuesday that he won't return until next week at the earliest. It's a testament to the Dodgers' depth that they're still a very good team, even with all these problems, and the promotion of top prospect Josue De Paula has already paid off. But these are very real and significant injury issues to key players, and the timeline to get them all back is compressed, to say the least. Securing a first-round bye would give them a few extra days’ rest before starting the NLDS, but Ohtani, Pages, Diaz, Freeman, Henriquez and Sasaki may either not play again during the regular season or make only a few at-bats or a single appearance before the playoffs. They’ve also turned Brice Turang, Andrew Vaughn and Jake Bauers into elite offensive contributors. With the Dodgers taking on water and big-name players like Mookie Betts, Will Smith, Freddie Freeman and Kyle Tucker well below their career averages, might this be the Brewers’ year? When they say you can't predict baseball, this is why.

articles.title: Pete Alonso hits career home run No. 300 at Mets' Citi Field, draws standing ovation and curtain call from his former home fans
articles.summary: Several fans wearing Mets jerseys stood up and greeted Alonso's achievement with an ovation.
articles.body:
Pete Alonso's first game back at Citi Field on Monday night since leaving the New York Mets for the Baltimore Orioles was an emotional one.

On Tuesday, he punctuated the homecoming with a significant career milestone. In the second game of the series between the Mets and Orioles, Alonso hit the 300th home run of his career. And Mets fans cheered him like he was still playing for the home team.

Alonso hit the solo shot in the top of the ninth inning. And despite tying the game at 3-3, Alonso's shot received an ovation from the Mets fans in the stands.

The home run ultimately sent the game to extra innings, where Alonso's Orioles secured a 7-5 win in 11.

Alonso spent his first seven MLB seasons playing for the Mets and hit 264 of his now 300 home runs in a New York uniform. He was one of baseball's most exciting sluggers throughout his Mets tenure and remains beloved in New York, as evidenced by his warm welcome this week.

Fans arrived at Citi Field on Monday with signs greeting Alonso, with one reading "We Miss You Pete!" The Mets greeted him with a tribute on the video board, and the crowd serenaded him with a chant and multiple standing ovations.

Alonso's former Mets teammates, including Francisco Lindor , joined in on the ovation when Alonso took the plate for his first at-bat. Alonso reciprocated the love by removing his helmet and acknowledging the crowd.

Alonso went hitless Monday night, but his Orioles left the game with a 2-1 victory.

On Tuesday, he delivered with the home-run power that made him a beloved figure in Queens.

While Alonso was a linchpin in New York's lineup for the better part of a decade, the Mets didn't prioritize signing him to a new contract as they revamped their roster in hopes of competing for a World Series this season. He reportedly didn't receive a formal offer for a contract extension and left last winter to sign a a five-year, $155 million deal with the Orioles.

New York's roster revamp hasn't worked out. The Mets entered Tuesday's game in last place in the NL East at 69-81 and already eliminated from the playoffs after Monday night's loss .

Mets fans, meanwhile, understand that the decision to leave wasn't necessarily Alonso's and have shown him lots of love during his stint back at Citi Field. He gave them more to cheer for Tuesday night than the Mets have for most of the season.

articles.title: MLB fans have no sympathy for Mets as Pete Alonso slams 300th career home run at Citi Field
articles.summary: Things have gone from bad to worse for the New York Mets. After the Baltimore Orioles knocked them out of playoff contention, now their own former star has r...
articles.body:
Things have gone from bad to worse for the New York Mets . After the Baltimore Orioles knocked them out of playoff contention, now their own former star has reached a milestone against them.

Fans of the New York Mets might genuinely be the strongest people in all of sports. The team is currently experiencing another disappointing MLB regular season.

Despite having names like Juan Soto , Bo Bichette , and Francisco Lindor on the payroll, the Mets have failed to qualify for the playoffs for the second year in a row.

Now, Pete Alonso has returned to his old stomping grounds at Citi Field. And true to form, the 2025 Silver Slugger Award winner has reached a major career landmark against the Mets.

Pete Alonso hits his 300th career home run at Citi Field and MLB fans are roasting the Mets for it

Playing against the Mets on Tuesday night, Alonso hit his first home run as a visiting player at Citi Field. With his team trailing 2-3, Alonso smashed one out of the park to tie the score up at 3-3.

The Orioles went on to win 7-5. The homer was Alonso's 124th at the ballpark, he hit 123 for the Mets there before this one. Despite their former legend hitting his 300th home run against New York, other fans had no sympathy for the Mets.

"The Mets franchise is a complete disgrace," wrote one fan. "Could there have been a more fitting venue for Alonso to reach this milestone?" another fan questioned.

"It's sad to see that Mets fans are cheering for Pete hitting a nuke while wearing a different jersey," a third fan commented. "Man, that was the biggest **** you to Stearns," another added.

"The Mets need to feel real shame at this very moment," claimed a fifth fan. "Good for you Pete. Mets organization deserves this," said a sixth comment.

For Mets fans who are already suffering, this was an unnecessary further blow to their mood. They will have an entire offseason to lick their wounds and hope somehow for a better year in 2027.

articles.title: Guardians News: Vogt manages like he needs W; Smith and Rocchio deliver
articles.summary: For the second straight day (they might be on #3 by the time you read this) the White Sox went with a tried-and-true Guardian-dominating strategy: They start...
articles.body:
For the second straight day (they might be on #3 by the time you read this) the White Sox went with a tried-and-true Guardian-dominating strategy: They started a left-handed relief pitcher.

But Chris Murphy was terrible. Adell & Bazzana hit b2b jacks off him and things were looking good. But as usual, the Guards did nothing against the "bulk" pitcher—one run was because he threw errantly to first base and drilled the helmeted umpire with his bouncy projectile.

The sleepy offense might have been enough, but Craig Yoho 's attempts to find the strike zone Only Lived Once and Hunter Gaddis couldn't miss any bats.

Steve Vogt managed this game like he should have—like winning it would possibly earn him a 1st round playoff bye eventually—and got Sabrowski , Gaddis and Cade Smith in way earlier than usual. Cade was awesome and kept things close for our September and October hero Brayan Rocchio .

• the Blue Jays wet themselves against Detroit

• Orioles won . We call this naquinmaxxng .
